title: Partnership and LLC accounting
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 4 guide matches, 23 question matches, 15 assessment matches, and 35 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: Are book capital, section 704(b) capital, tax-basis capital, and outside basis distinct?
questions.finding: Tax measures remain distinct: §743(b) creates transferee-only partnership-property basis and tax-item adjustments; it does not change common inside basis or the transferee’s capital account. That answers the tax-basis distinction, not GAAP equity presentation.
questions.remaining_gap: Current US GAAP partnership presentation and partner-specific ledger/liability facts remain open.

questions.question: How do cash/noncash contributions and built-in gain/loss affect capital and later allocations?
questions.finding: A’s contributed property carries a $6,000 initial built-in gain; after first-year tax depreciation, a $9,000 year-two sale sends $5,400 gain to A. If AB then liquidates with $19,000 cash, A has $9,400 basis and $100 gain while B has $9,600 basis and $100 loss.
questions.remaining_gap: The example is tax regulation, not client facts or a GAAP capital-account policy; agreement method choice and special 704(c) rules remain.

questions.question: How are profits/losses allocated and midyear admissions/exits handled?
questions.finding: Prior sources still describe agreement-based allocations and varying-interest rules; this pass adds no new midyear-admission or safe-harbor evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual allocations, admission/exit dates, agreement and applicable tax-year elections remain entity-specific.

questions.question: How do distributions, withdrawals, liability relief, and service payments affect partners?
questions.finding: General tax routes distinguish §734(b) common-basis adjustment from §743(b) transferee-only basis; §736 classifies full-interest retirement payments and §736(b)(2)-(3) has conditional receivables/goodwill scope.
questions.remaining_gap: Complex noncash/liability distributions and service payments require the actual facts, agreement, partner/entity status and current-year tax law.

questions.question: How are transfers, retirement, liquidation and windup represented?
questions.finding: General tax mechanics now separate a third-party transfer from partnership liquidation payments, distinguish §736(a) from §736(b), and reconcile final distributions to outside basis; the proposed windup schedule keeps tax and book measures separate.
questions.remaining_gap: The question also asks how windup is represented: US GAAP presentation, legal transfer/windup rights, member status, and agreement-specific allocation/payment terms remain unresolved.

recommended_additions: Add a dedicated role- and accounting-basis-specific guide using the scope and reconciliations in the brief.
Add a worked 704(c) multiyear schedule ending in liquidation, with outside-basis and §731/§732 reconciliation.
Add conditional §736 treatment and §734/§743 election/mandatory-trigger distinctions; keep GAAP equity and agreement rights separate.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: Partnership structures are common across investment, real-estate, operating and family-office entities; book capital, tax capital and outside basis are commonly conflated.

title: Fund accounting and investment partnerships
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 10 guide matches, 31 question matches, 32 assessment matches, and 59 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How should a US fund close distinguish portfolio assets/NAV, investor capital, manager/GP, and portfolio-company books?
questions.finding: Prior ASC 946 and custody materials already distinguish fund assets/NAV and investor capital from GP/manager and portfolio-company reporting; this pass reinforces the boundary but adds no new consolidation evidence.
questions.remaining_gap: ASC 810 and legal title/control require the actual structure, contracts, and ledger.

questions.question: What valuation evidence supports private investment fair value and NAV?
questions.finding: BDO’s 2018 discussion of a working draft adds a general calibration and security-class method framework, but current authoritative security-class guidance is unverified and entity-specific value remains open.
questions.remaining_gap: The source is a nonauthoritative 2018 discussion of an AICPA working draft; current authoritative security-class guidance, actual class rights, transaction orderliness, measurement-date inputs and professional valuation remain unverified; IPEV remains excluded.

questions.question: How should commitments, capital calls, distributions and unfunded commitments reconcile?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA notice examples and IRS tax reporting sources already provide the general call/distribution/unfunded commitment reconciliation scope.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual commitment terms, call types, subsequent changes and unusual distributions remain agreement-dependent.

questions.question: How do carried-interest fees versus profit allocations affect fund, GP, and manager statements?
questions.finding: Fund class allocation and manager carry revenue are separate questions. FASB staff’s 2020 view is that service-compensation carry is within Topic 606 regardless of cash/equity form; KPMG’s 2025 interpretation of the 2016 TRG/SEC Observer comments allows a consistent ownership model on specific facts with full ASC 810/323 analysis. Ares used ASC 323 for carry and ASC 606 for incentive fees in 2018.
questions.remaining_gap: Not a universal policy choice or Board-level conclusion. Reporting-entity structure, contract substance, variable-consideration reversal, clawback, consolidation/equity-method facts and current Codification remain necessary.

questions.question: How do custody, investor delivery, and regulatory audit duties interact?
questions.finding: Custody, audit, investor delivery and adviser obligations remain a separate regulatory analysis from fund accounting.
questions.remaining_gap: Current adviser and pool status, custody, audit exception, delivery dates, Form PF/CFTC/ERISA facts and later legal developments require current review.

questions.question: How should ASC 946 fund financial statements present net assets, class NAV/capital activity, subscriptions, and realized/unrealized performance?
questions.finding: Prior ASC 946 technical material already supports the general fund financial-statement and class-capital presentation path.
questions.remaining_gap: Registered-fund requirements and applicable statement set depend on fund status and reporting facts; current Codification review remains.

questions.question: How are management fees, fee waivers, expense limitations, and offsets presented in an ASC 946 fund?
questions.finding: Fund management-fee expense/waiver/offset accounting is distinct from the manager’s contract revenue. The new manager-side evidence treats separate management services under Topic 606 while analyzing carried interest independently as service compensation or a possible equity ownership arrangement.
questions.remaining_gap: Fund fee terms, waiver/expense-cap mechanics, offsets, consolidation, manager contract and ledger remain unreviewed.

questions.question: How should contractual waterfall distributions sequence return of capital, preferred return, catch-up, carry and clawback?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA model LPA shows one waterfall sequence and bracketed alternatives; it remains an illustration, not a universal distribution rule.
questions.remaining_gap: No actual waterfall, side letters, preferred-return basis, clawback or realized/unrealized ledger was inspected.

questions.question: How do hedge high-water marks, classes/series and side pockets affect investor NAV and incentive allocations?
questions.finding: Historical Irish/practitioner methods explain HWM equalization alternatives, but general side-pocket mechanics and private-partnership subscription entries are not fully resolved.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual side-pocket participation, dealing NAV, fee reversals, HWM, crystallization, and private-partnership subscription accounting depend on fund contracts and administrator records; the guide is historical Irish practice, not US authority.

questions.question: How do ASC 946 investor-class allocations reflect unrealized marks, carried interest and clawback at the reporting date?
questions.finding: ASC 946 fund-class allocation of marks, fees and carry is not the same reporting question as the GP/manager’s carry revenue or investment. The latter may involve Topic 606 or a fact-supported ownership model under interpretive sources.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual fund agreement, carry classification in GP/manager statements, clawback and participant compensation require entity-specific analysis and current GAAP review.

questions.question: How should ASC 946 subscription equalization and class capital transactions be reflected?
questions.finding: Hedge-fund share equalization must preserve each subscriber’s issue NAV/HWM and accrued-fee position, but these administrator methods do not answer the ASC 946 entry or private partnership subscription equalization amount.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual subscription ledger, LPA, administrator method, retroactive NAV adjustments and current ASC 946 treatment remain open.

recommended_additions: Add a focused ASC 946 fund financial-statement and close guide using KPMG’s current public technical handbook as interpretive context; clearly distinguish authority from professional interpretation.
Add a separate waterfall/carry schedule branch linked to a model LPA and actual fund-document inputs, plus a hedge classes/series/equalization/side-pocket branch using illustrative statements.
Retain the restricted IPEV lead as discovery-only pending a rights review; do not carry forward substantive claims.
Map fund, GP, manager and portfolio-company reporting as separate reporting entities.
Show the manager carry service-revenue versus ownership analysis and hedge equalization methods separately from ASC 946 fund-class entries.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
IPEV remains a rights-restricted discovery lead only; its substantive text is excluded and no valuation claim is based on it.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: Fund reporting crosses legal entities, NAV, investor capital, adviser fees and regulatory custody; available corpus routes are fragmented.

title: Private equity, venture capital, and hedge funds
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 9 guide matches, 36 question matches, 19 assessment matches, and 54 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How do PE/VC valuation and recent-round calibration support fair value by security class?
questions.finding: BDO’s 2018 working-draft interpretation expands the unit-of-account, calibration and model-selection map; current authoritative security-class guidance and any specific valuation remain unverified.
questions.remaining_gap: Current authoritative security-class/fair-value guidance remains unverified; the BDO source summarizes a 2018 working draft, and actual rights, inputs and valuation require case-specific analysis; IPEV remains excluded.

questions.question: How do calls, distributions, unfunded commitments and investor notices reconcile?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA and IRS materials already support call, distribution, unfunded-commitment and investor-notice reconciliation.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual LPA and unusual call/distribution rights remain untested.

questions.question: How are preferred return, catch-up, carry, escrow and clawback modeled?
questions.finding: Prior ILPA model LPA gives one preferred-return/catch-up/carry/clawback illustration; no new waterfall evidence was added.
questions.remaining_gap: Escrow, clawback security, whole-fund versus deal-by-deal waterfall and actual carry terms remain agreement-specific.

questions.question: How do fund and adviser reporting requirements differ after the 2023 rule vacatur?
questions.finding: Prior SEC vacatur and custody/Form PF sources remain the basis for the bounded fund/adviser regulatory distinction.
questions.remaining_gap: Recheck adviser-specific custody, filing thresholds, CFTC/ERISA status and rule changes for the relevant date.

questions.question: How should hedge fund dealing NAV, high-water marks, equalization and side pockets be computed?
questions.finding: Historical Irish administrator/practitioner materials describe investor capital accounts, series accounting and equalization methods each preserve HWM/cohort fee history differently. A historical 2009 Irish administrator guide gives a $1,000 credit example and the brief derives a labeled later-$107 comparison.
questions.remaining_gap: Method selection, actual dealing NAV, fee reversals, side-pocket participation, crystallization, and redemption terms require the actual fund documents and administrator records.

questions.question: What does a new JV recognize at formation, and what is distinct for venturer accounting?
questions.finding: Prior FASB joint-venture formation source supports the effective-date and formation-versus-venturer-accounting distinction.
questions.remaining_gap: Investor’s subsequent control/equity-method analysis remains separate and fact-dependent.

questions.question: How do fund NAV and investor capital allocations reflect unrealized marks, fees, carry and clawback under ASC 946?
questions.finding: The fund’s ASC 946 investor-class allocation of fair-value changes, expenses and carry must be kept separate from a GP/manager’s carried-interest reporting as service revenue or an ownership interest.
questions.remaining_gap: The actual agreement determines the class allocation and carry amount; precise current ASC 946 treatment and GP/manager method remain to verify.

questions.question: How should new subscriptions/redemptions and class/series equalization be tracked?
questions.finding: Series/equalization structures explain how a new subscription can avoid bearing pre-entry appreciation fees, but they do not prescribe the ASC 946 transaction entry for a private partnership.
questions.remaining_gap: New-subscription pricing, share/interest issuance, retrospective equalization and redemption rights depend on LPA/PPM and actual subledger; GAAP entry not established.

recommended_additions: Add separate PE/VC waterfall/carry and hedge class/series/equalization/side-pocket question paths, supported by model and illustrative materials but gated on actual LPA/PPM terms.

Use KPMG ASC 946 and hedge financial-statement examples as clearly attributed technical interpretations and examples; preserve security-level private valuation calibration as an open research question.
Do not reuse substantive IPEV content; retain only its restricted discovery status pending rights review.
Add a class-level private-investment valuation calibration worksheet tied to rights and measurement-date facts.
Compare equalization-credit/deposit, contingent-liquidation, investor-account and share-series methods; keep subscription and HWM terms explicit.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
IPEV valuation content remains restricted and is not used; private security calibration remains an open question.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: PE/VC/hedge fund allocation, valuation and performance fee mechanics have material investor-reporting consequences and are absent from current dedicated guides.

title: Real estate ownership and property management
baseline_status: Adjacent / partial screening matches; no adequacy conclusion
baseline_summary: Inclusive baseline: 4 guide matches, 21 question matches, 13 assessment matches, and 28 linked source records. Matches are shared/adjacent and do not prove depth or sufficiency.

questions.question: How should owner, developer, manager, broker, contractor and REIT roles route?
questions.finding: California provides a bounded role/accounting route when a licensed broker handles another person’s property-management funds: the broker must maintain trust-fund and separate beneficiary records and respect trust-fund deposit/disbursement rules. This does not define roles or law nationwide.
questions.remaining_gap: Owner/developer/manager/broker/contractor/REIT roles depend on entity chart, ownership, contracts, state licensing and law; the California broker rule does not cover every manager.

questions.question: How should acquisition and development costs, CIP, placed-in-service, depreciation, and sale be separated?
questions.finding: Prior EY/KPMG and IRS sources already address development cost capitalization, book/tax depreciation and disposal; this pass adds no new cost guidance.
questions.remaining_gap: Property-use facts, component costs, acquired operating property, tax depreciation and exact current GAAP application remain.

questions.question: How should rent, incentives, deposits, and lease components flow through a rent roll?
questions.finding: Secondary GAAP interpretation describes operating-lessor straight-line rent when collection is probable, variable rent on occurrence/collection as applicable, and separates refundable deposits, nonrefundable consideration and deposit retention; IRS Pub. 527 separately treats refundable deposits and advance rent for tax.
questions.remaining_gap: Lease incentives, components/CAM and actual deposit rights require lease/state law facts; tax timing differs from book treatment; exact current Codification application remains.

questions.question: How should CAM/tenant recoveries reconcile and present?
questions.finding: Prior Deloitte lessor-reimbursement/CAM sources already support the bounded accounting route.
questions.remaining_gap: Actual lease terms, expedients, expense true-ups and allocation remain unreviewed.

questions.question: How should property-manager cash collection and owner settlement reconcile?
questions.finding: California’s 2026 broker rules require receipt/disbursement control records, separate beneficiary/transaction ledgers, monthly ledger-to-control reconciliation and written consent for a disbursement that would create a trust-fund shortfall. This supplies a jurisdiction-specific custody-accounting floor. A separate owner statement/remittance formula remains contract-dependent; the proposed property settlement schedule is an editorial control.
questions.remaining_gap: The regulations do not establish a national rule or the contractual timing/calculation of owner remittances. Determine broker/license status, state/local law, agency and trust terms, owner approvals, fee rights, bank activity and tenant liabilities from the actual engagement.

questions.question: What current federal REIT qualification data is needed?
questions.finding: The inspected Code and 2025 IRS instructions provide a general REIT threshold checklist, but the question asks for current qualification data and full consolidation-through date, attribution/look-through, TRS and cure details remain open.
questions.remaining_gap: GovInfo display did not show its consolidation-through date; 2025 instructions are not 2026 instructions. Verify the year’s statute, regulations, attribution/look-through, TRS, cure and current return requirements before concluding qualification.

recommended_additions: Expand the US real-estate guide with current ASC 970 development cost, ASC 842/606 lessor/CAM, real-estate seller revenue, and property-manager fee examples from EY, KPMG and Deloitte.

Add an owner/developer/manager reconciliation workbook outline that separates lease revenue, service fees, deposits, CAM billings/true-ups, project costs, tax basis and REIT tests; label control recommendations as editorial.
Keep state/local tenant-protection and property-manager trust/custody obligations as jurisdiction-specific open branches.
Add a role/basis map and a rent-roll bridge separating GAAP rent, tax rent, recoveries, deposits and liabilities.
Add a suggested manager-to-owner settlement control and a current-year REIT test data request; label controls as editorial and test status as date-dependent.
unresolved_gaps: No professional accounting review was performed.
No entity-specific contracts, ledger data, or state-by-state legal/tax analysis were available.
Current Codification wording and entity-specific application remain to be checked; this follow-up does not infer that current ASC verification requires paid access.
priority_rationale: Owners, developers, managers and REITs have different book/tax/legal bases; existing coverage is partial and includes historical accounting standards.
